title: Mysticism
author: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
supports: Mysticism, experience, interpretation, ineffability and noetic claims.
limitations: Selected sections reviewed; definitions vary across traditions.

title: Pseudo-Dionysius the Areopagite
author: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
supports: Apophatic and kataphatic theology; divine names and limits of language.
limitations: Christian theological context; not a generic occult dictionary.

title: Ibn Arabi
author: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
supports: Imaginal reality, imagination and barzakh in Ibn Arabi.
limitations: Selected philosophical sections reviewed; does not represent every Sufi school.

title: Plotinus
author: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
supports: The One, Intellect and metaphysical procession.
limitations: Selected sections reviewed; philosophical claims described, not endorsed as measurements.

title: Proclus
author: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
supports: Theurgy and late Platonist approaches to divine assimilation.
limitations: Section 3.6 reviewed.

title: Marsilio Ficino
author: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
supports: Renaissance Platonism and reception of ancient theology.
limitations: Overview reviewed; no claims of uninterrupted ancient lineage.

title: Gnosticism
author: Internet Encyclopedia of Philosophy
supports: Gnosis, aeons, Sophia, pleroma and demiurge in selected systems.
limitations: An interpretive overview of diverse movements, not a uniform creed.

title: Great Burkhan Khaldun Mountain and its surrounding sacred landscape
author: UNESCO World Heritage Centre
supports: Sacred landscape, worship traditions, ovoo and documented restrictions.
limitations: Nomination-era heritage description; not a current visitor-permission or legal guide.

title: Spellbound: Magic, Ritual & Witchcraft
author: Ashmolean Museum, University of Oxford
supports: Material objects and historical European magical beliefs.
limitations: Exhibition ran in 2018–2019; supports object history, not supernatural efficacy.

title: The World Bewitch'd: Introduction
author: Cornell University Library
supports: Witchcraft accusations, persecution and historical evidence.
limitations: Accusations are not proof that the accused practiced magic.

title: Three Books of Occult Philosophy, Book I, part 1
author: Heinrich Cornelius Agrippa; English translation 1651; digital edition Joseph H. Peterson
supports: Natural magic, elements and hidden properties in Renaissance cosmology.
limitations: Historical text; modern editorial notes and transcriptions have separate rights.

title: Three Books of Occult Philosophy, Book II, part 1
author: Heinrich Cornelius Agrippa; English translation 1651; digital edition Joseph H. Peterson
supports: Number symbolism and mathematical magic.
limitations: A historical belief system; numerology is not statistical inference.

title: Three Books of Occult Philosophy, Book II, part 2
author: Heinrich Cornelius Agrippa; English translation 1651; digital edition Joseph H. Peterson
supports: Numerical correspondences, letters and celestial symbolism.
limitations: Selected passages reviewed; do not treat correspondences as universal.

title: Three Books of Occult Philosophy, Book III, part 1
author: Heinrich Cornelius Agrippa; English translation 1651; digital edition Joseph H. Peterson
supports: Religious magic, secrecy and restrictions on disclosure.
limitations: Chapter II especially; author's reports about other cultures require independent verification.

title: Lemegeton, Part 1: Goetia
author: Historical manuscripts; digital edition Joseph H. Peterson
supports: Spirit catalogues, seals, circles, conjuration and dismissal.
limitations: Literary and historical reference; no claim that spirits or coercive rites work.

title: Emerald Tablet of Hermes: Translations
author: Historical translations collected by Internet Sacred Text Archive
supports: Upper/lower correspondence and alchemical imagery.
limitations: Composite page includes modern translations and commentary; no bulk text copied.

title: The Sophic Hydrolith, in The Hermetic Museum, Volume I
author: Historical alchemical tract; A. E. Waite English edition, 1893
supports: Black, white and red stages; dissolution, condensation and allegory.
limitations: Historical chemical and religious claims are not instructions or verified remedies.

title: The Golden Tract Concerning the Stone of the Philosophers
author: Historical alchemical tract; A. E. Waite English edition, 1893
supports: Philosophers' stone, concealment, allegory and claims to secret knowledge.
limitations: Historical rhetoric is evidence of what authors claimed, not proof of transmutation.

title: The Kybalion, Chapter II: The Seven Hermetic Principles
author: Three Initiates, 1908
supports: Mentalism, correspondence, vibration, polarity, rhythm, cause/effect and gender.
limitations: Modern occult publication; not evidence of an ancient Egyptian seven-law syllabus.

title: Thelema
author: Ordo Templi Orientis, U.S. Grand Lodge
supports: Thelema, Crowley, individual Will and Magick.
limitations: Represents the organization’s own introductory account.

title: What Is Druidry?
author: Order of Bards, Ovates & Druids
supports: Contemporary Druidry, creativity, nature and wisdom.
limitations: Represents this order; does not establish all ancient Druid practices.

title: Wicca
author: Harvard University, The Pluralism Project
supports: Wicca as a stream of contemporary Paganism.
limitations: Short overview; insufficient for universal rules about Wiccan practice.

title: Tarot
author: Wikipedia contributors
supports: Italian playing-card history and later occult use.
limitations: Orientation only; historical dates should receive specialist checking before a scholarly publication.

title: Rider–Waite Tarot
author: Wikipedia contributors
supports: A. E. Waite, Pamela Colman Smith and the 1909 deck.
limitations: Use alongside Waite's primary text; modern editions may differ.

title: Tarot of Marseilles
author: Wikipedia contributors
supports: Marseille deck family, pip structure and ordering.
limitations: A family of decks, not one canonical edition.

title: Thoth Tarot
author: Wikipedia contributors
supports: Crowley/Harris deck, renamed trumps and courts.
limitations: Comparison only; not a production-ready astrological correspondence table.

title: Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn
author: Wikipedia contributors
supports: Modern initiatory order and occult synthesis.
limitations: High-level orientation; internal teachings differ across later organizations.

title: Kabbalah
author: Wikipedia contributors
supports: Jewish Kabbalah, sefirot and distinction from later adaptations.
limitations: Educational draft; consult Jewish scholarship before publishing detailed teachings.

title: Tapu in Polynesian cultures
author: Wikipedia contributors
supports: Sacred restrictions and the background of the English word taboo.
limitations: Local meanings differ; community-specific review needed.

title: The Pictorial Key to the Tarot
author: A. E. Waite, 1910/1911 editions; designs by Pamela Colman Smith
supports: Structure of this tarot reference and chapter navigation.
limitations: The 78 card pages below belong to this same work, not 78 independent authorities.

title: The Pictorial Key: The Tarot in History
author: A. E. Waite
supports: Waite's own critique of speculative tarot origin stories.
limitations: Historical scholarship has developed since Waite; not the final authority on origins.

title: The Pictorial Key: Greater Arcana Divinatory Meanings
author: A. E. Waite
supports: Historical predictive meanings, including alarming and gendered formulations.
limitations: Preserved as context; Od Toirog interpretations deliberately do not reproduce those judgments.

title: The Pictorial Key: An Ancient Celtic Method of Divination
author: A. E. Waite
supports: Ten-card cross spread and optional significator.
limitations: The word ancient in the chapter title is an authorial claim, not established Celtic provenance.

title: Chaos magic
author: Wikipedia contributors
supports: Modern sigil practice, instrumental belief and the specialized use of gnosis.
limitations: Orientation only; references to physics within occult systems do not validate the systems scientifically.

title: Egregore
author: Wikipedia contributors
supports: Modern group thought-form concept and earlier different uses.
limitations: No claim that a collective entity has been observed.

title: Theosophy
author: Wikipedia contributors
supports: Modern Theosophy and its esoteric cosmology.
limitations: Distinguish modern appropriations from the religions they reference.

title: Akashic records
author: Wikipedia contributors
supports: Theosophical belief in an immaterial record.
limitations: Not a searchable empirical archive or verified account of a user's past lives.

title: Sigil
author: Wikipedia contributors
supports: Historical seals and modern intention-symbol practices.
limitations: The meaning depends on the named system.

title: Divination
author: Wikipedia contributors
supports: Broad term and differences among divinatory media.
limitations: Brief terminology orientation; no efficacy conclusion follows from historical use.
